Archie vs Wix Symphony.

This is the closest comparison on the site. Both give you a team of agents in one chat, both act while you are away, and both check with you before the things that matter. The difference is whose computer the work happens on, and who picks the AI company that answers you.

Archie is in testing. The waitlist hears the day it opens. See where it stands → Checked against the sources below on September 11, 2026.

The short answer

A phone you sign in from, or a computer you switch on.

Symphony is a service you reach with a Wix account, in a browser or its iOS and Android appSource 1. Archie is a program that runs on a computer of your own, and talks to the AI company on an account of your own. Both of those buy real things, and they are close to opposites. Most of what follows is downstream of that one choice.

Symphony suits you if

  • You want it working with every computer you own switched off
  • You run your business from a phone, and want your agents there tooSource 1
  • You want a free start that renews every monthSource 2
  • You would rather one company handled the AI choice for you
  • You want it today: Symphony is live and Archie is still in testing

Archie suits you if

  • You would rather your files and conversations stayed on a computer you can unplugSource 4
  • Your account passwords belong in your own computer’s password storeSource 4
  • You want your pick of 7 AI companies, switchable whenever you likeSource 4
  • You would rather pay the AI company at cost than buy an allowance
  • You need to be able to say where a client’s work sat, and point at the code that makes the answer trueSource 4
Side by side

Row by row.

Archie compared with Symphony by Wix, across where you reach it, whose computer the work happens on, which AI answers, approvals, how it is metered, what an account requires, and cost.
  Archie Symphony by Wix
Where you reach it The Archie app on your Mac or Windows computer, and from your phone through a chat app you connect: Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix, or iMessage on a Mac A browser, or the iOS and Android app: “Symphony is available on iOS and Android”Source 1
Whose computer the work happens on Yours. The agent runs on your computer while it is awake, and your conversations go to the AI company directly, on your accountSource 4 Not yours, and Wix does not publish where. Their pages say how you reach it and what it does, not what it runs onSource 1
Which AI answers you Your pick of 7: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Groq, xAI, DeepSeek or Mistral, or any provider of your own that speaks the OpenAI format. Changeable laterSource 4 “Powered by Wix AI”Source 1. No model is named and no choice is offered on their product or pricing pages
Does it ask before it acts Yes, in two places, and neither is a setting anyone can switch off. A calendar change is proposed and applied only after you approve it in a later message. An email reply is a draft, and nothing leaves your account until you send it or set a timeSource 4 Yes: it “checks with you first before your agents act, so nothing important happens without your approval”Source 1
How the AI is metered You pay the AI company directly, at their price, billed to you and capped by you. We never see it. Measured at $1 to $7 a month for a handful of tasks a daySource 5 AI credits: “the exact amount is calculated after each action, based on its complexity and the tool used”. They reset monthly and do not roll overSource 2
What runs out Nothing, on your own AI account: you are buying usage at cost, so heavier months cost more rather than stopping The credits. “Your team of agents takes a breather until your credits renew”, with work and history keptSource 2
What an account needs An Otian account, an account with one of the 7 AI companies, and a computer you can leave on and connectedSource 4 A Wix account, though no Wix website: “You use Symphony with a Wix account”Source 1
Cost $30 a month or $299 a year when it ships, plus the AI billed to you at cost. Or $59 a month with $25 of AI inside itSource 5 Free, then Basic $16 a month ($12.80 annually), Pro $40 ($32), Max $80 ($64)Source 2

Symphony’s figures read from Wix’s own pages on September 11, 2026; sources at the foot of the page. The two price columns are not like for like and we are not going to pretend they are. Symphony’s number is the whole bill. Archie’s plain plan is two bills, ours and the AI company’s, and the second one is yours to watch and cap. The plan with the AI included is the one bill, for the person who would rather not think about it; on that one your agent will not read email or watch texts, because those carry what other people wrote and the AI runs on our account.

Where Symphony wins

Five things it does that we do not.

All five are real, and we are not expecting to take any of them back soon.

It works with everything you own switched off

Symphony keeps going whether or not you have a computer on, because the work is not happening on a computer of yours. Archie answers while your computer is awake and Archie is running. Shut the lid and it waits until the lid opens, so a briefing due at seven needs the computer awake at seven. If nothing you own can be left on, that settles it, and what to run it on is the honest version of what we would be asking you to buy.

It starts free, and keeps starting free

500 credits a month and 100 a day, with no card asked for, renewing every monthSource 2. Archie asks for no card either and we pay for the AI to begin with, but ours is a trial and not a tier: it ends when the credits or the 14 days do. If you want to run something indefinitely at no cost, theirs does that and ours does not.

It is built for a phone first

A “mobile-first interface”Source 1, downloaded from an app store, running the same wherever you are. Archie reaches your phone through a chat app you connect, which works well and is a step to set up, and the computer it thinks on is still at home. For someone who runs their business from a phone in a van, that is their design and not ours.

Nothing to run, and nothing to keep running

No computer to leave on, no operating system updates to survive, nothing to plug back in after a power cut. Wix carries all of that. With Archie, the computer is yours, which is the point of it and also a thing you now own.

You can have it today

Symphony is live on iOS, Android and the webSource 1. Archie is in testing, and the waitlist hears the day that changes. If you need something running this week, that is not us yet.

Worth saying

Two questions worth asking either of us.

Where does the work happen? Ours is answerable to the packet: the agent runs on your computer, your conversations go to the AI company you picked on your own account, and no server of ours is in that path. Two exceptions, both ours and both named: the free starter credits and the plan with the AI included run on our Anthropic account, so while you are on either, what you write passes through our server on the way to Anthropic. Nothing writes it down, we keep no copy, and none of it is used for anythingSource 4. Wix does not publish where Symphony’s agents run, so we are not going to tell you either. We are telling you the question has an answer on our side and that you can check it yourselfSource 4.

Which mind is answering? Symphony is “powered by Wix AI”Source 1, with no model named and no choice offered, so that decision is made once by Wix for everybody. Their case for it is being “built on 20 years of real business expertise”Source 1, drawn from “supporting hundreds of millions of businesses worldwide”Source 3. That is a genuine thing to offer, and it is worth being plain about what it is: an average of what businesses like yours tend to do. Archie starts from whichever of the 7 you pick and learns your specifics from the files and instructions you give it, on your computer. Pick on purpose, either way.

And one thing that is the same on both sides, so nobody reads this page and concludes otherwise. Symphony checks with you before its agents act, in its own words and by its own designSource 1. So does Archie. Asking first is not the thing that separates us, and anyone telling you it is has not read their page.

Sources for every figure and claim on this page
1Symphony by Wix: what it is and how you reach it

“With a mobile-first interface, it’s proactive, easy to use and connects to any tool or application.” “Symphony is available on iOS and Android. Download the app and take your business with you wherever you go.” It is “powered by Wix AI and built on 20 years of real business expertise”, and the page names no model and offers no model choice. From wix.com/symphony. The Wix account requirement (“Yes, Symphony is a Wix product. You use Symphony with a Wix account”, and “You don’t need a Wix website”) and the approval sentence (“Symphony keeps you in control. It checks with you first before your agents act, so nothing important happens without your approval”) are from Symphony: An Overview. Both read on September 11, 2026. Wix does not publish where Symphony’s agents run, on either page or in the launch announcement, so this page says how you reach it and does not guess at the rest.

2Symphony’s prices and its credits

Free, then Basic at $16 a month ($12.80 billed annually), Pro at $40 ($32) and Max at $80 ($64). “Start on the free plan, no credit card needed.” The free plan carries 500 monthly credits and 100 daily credits; Basic carries 2,000 and Pro 5,000, and Max publishes no figure. Credits “reset monthly and do not roll over”, and the unit is defined on the page as: “Each action you take with agents and tools consumes AI credits. The exact amount is calculated after each action, based on its complexity and the tool used.” When they run out, “your team of agents takes a breather until your credits renew. Nothing gets lost.” From wix.com/symphony/pricing, read on September 11, 2026. The daily cap was 50 when we first read this page on August 24 and is 100 now, which is worth knowing if you are comparing against anything written earlier, ours included.

3Wix’s launch announcement

Symphony described as “a new standalone AI agent platform”, “platform-agnostic, supporting any business whether they use Wix, another platform, or do not yet have a website”, and drawing on “experience and unique data accumulated in supporting hundreds of millions of businesses worldwide”. From the Wix press room, read on September 11, 2026. We print the reach figure as Wix’s claim about Wix; it is not our count and we have not verified it.

4Archie’s side of the table

The custody claim, the two exceptions where our own server is in the path, the password-store claim, the 7 AI companies, the 5 chat apps, and the approval gates that cannot be switched off are all on our Trust page, each pointing at the code that makes it true, with instructions for watching the traffic yourself. What you need to run it is on How It Works.

5Archie’s prices, and the $1 to $7

Our own prices, and our own measured figure for light AI use (a handful of tasks a day), both broken down on the pricing page, which also works through what a heavier day costs. The meter is yours to watch and cap.

What we have not claimed

Nothing here says Symphony is careless with your data: Wix documents its own controls and approvals and we quote them doing it. Nothing here says Symphony cannot do something because their marketing page did not mention it, which is a shortcut we have banned ourselves from taking. And we have not told you where their agents run, because they have not published it and guessing would be the same mistake in the other direction. Wix’s own security documentation is the place to judge their side properly.
